claims.text: Urbanisation is an increase in the proportion of a population living in urban areas; distinguish it from an increase in urban population alone.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Urban share is urban population divided by total population, multiplied by 100; a larger urban number does not prove a larger share.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Rural–urban migration, different rates of natural population change and changes in settlement classification can affect the urban share.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: People may move in response to rural constraints and perceived urban opportunities, but migration and urbanisation are not interchangeable concepts.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Many industrialised economies experienced substantial earlier rural–urban movement associated with industrial employment and service concentration.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Where a large share is already urban, further growth, suburban movement or movement away from city centres can follow different patterns.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Some developing economies experience rapid urban growth where migration and natural increase combine with a growing urban share.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: If housing, services and work opportunities expand more slowly than needs, existing access gaps can widen.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Rapid urban growth can place pressure on housing, water, sanitation, transport and employment where provision does not expand with needs.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Problems depend on service capacity, location and access as well as population numbers; residents are not themselves the cause of poor planning or exclusion.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Departure can reduce available rural labour or care support, while remittances and new connections can also support rural households.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: The net effect depends on who leaves, when work is needed, whether earnings are available and whether money or knowledge returns.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: When affordable housing and serviced land are insufficient, some residents build or occupy housing outside formal planning or tenure arrangements.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Informal settlements vary; inadequate infrastructure or insecure access can affect living conditions, but a settlement label does not describe every household.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Sanitation concerns safe management of human waste, and insufficient capacity can leave waste poorly contained or treated.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: When demand exceeds functioning provision, contamination of the living environment becomes a greater concern.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Water provision depends on a safe and accessible supply, functioning distribution and management of demand and contamination.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: A damaged or overloaded system can combine access difficulties with pollution risks where waste reaches the supply.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Transport connects residents with work and services, while communication supports access to information and coordination.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Growth at poorly connected edges can increase journey time and costs and limit the opportunities residents can actually reach.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Possible urban-growth responses include self-help housing, site-and-services schemes, rural development and planned new towns.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: These responses address different mechanisms and require resources, participation and continuing services; judge them by delivered access and functioning services.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Self-help housing involves residents contributing labour, decisions or resources to improve or build shelter, usually with suitable supporting arrangements.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: It may use local capability and staged improvements but can exclude people lacking time, physical capacity, finance or secure access.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: A site-and-services scheme provides planned plots with essential supporting services or access arrangements, with housing often developed in stages.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: It can address a serviced-land shortage, but affordability, location, secure usable access and continued service maintenance determine who benefits.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Rural development can improve livelihoods, services and opportunities in rural areas.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: It can expand genuine choices and reduce some pressures to migrate, but does not automatically reverse urbanisation or replace urban service provision.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: New towns are planned settlements intended to provide an organised location for housing, work and services.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: They can distribute activity and provide planned infrastructure, but require substantial coordination, finance and real links between homes, jobs and services.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Employment status concerns whether and how much someone works; formal or informal economic activity concerns institutional and regulatory arrangements.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: An informal economic activity is not an informal settlement, which describes a residential area; neither label alone determines a person’s employment status.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Unemployment is the situation of people without work who are available for and seeking work; exact statistical definitions depend on the source.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Underemployment means having work that uses less than a person’s available working time or productive capacity; it differs from having no work.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: Formal economic activity operates within the relevant recognised registration and regulatory arrangements; informal activity operates outside some of them.

verification.method: Original Codex teaching synthesis within approved source scope; pending independent Claude Code review.

claims.text: The exact statistical boundary depends on the source; informal does not by itself mean unemployed, illegal or located in an informal settlement.
